hub.speaker: Eloise
hub.text: Sit. Tea first. Then we'll talk about whatever brought you all this way.

text_variants.text: The craft listens better once the birds stop. Sit. There's tea in the pot yet.
You want the blight gone. I want what I'm owed. Sit. Tea first. There's honey if you take it.
Paid, one way or another. I don't ask which. Sit if you like, or don't — I've got stock for coin now too, if that suits you better than favors.
Mind the kettle, apprentice-of-no-one. The craft heard you. Pour before it whistles.

options.text: Let's not make this ugly. I'll broker fair terms. [Calming Touch]
What have you got, for coin instead of favors?
I've got a few things I don't need, myself. Buying?
The way you work — the craft. Could a person learn it?

options._comment: RIVERFARM CAPSTONE. On the HUB, not a chain tail, so an already-reported price_of_a_favor still reaches it on revisit. Gated on the quest TERMINAL, matching the other two spine stops. Deliberately NOT excluded on drove_off_collectors: the force path banks the same terminal, so gating her out would leave the spine unfinishable for fight players.
options.text: You've been sniffing at me since I came in. Go on.

options._comment: #396 closer. Appended last, and both counters are 0 in every shipped fixture, so no pinned hub array moves.

witch_ward_lore.speaker: Eloise
witch_ward_lore.text: Your door smells of a feeding ward. I keep one myself — smaller. Sit. If you're going to live over one, you'll learn what it eats.

witch_ward_taught._comment: HER OWN PIECE ONLY (spec 4): a hedge witch's feeding practice, scaled to her hollow. No seal, no lattice, no assembled picture -- she has never been under Liscor.
witch_ward_taught.speaker: Eloise
witch_ward_taught.text: Mine takes milk and a word, every seventh night. Yours was built to hold something that argues back, and a ward like that gets fed on purpose, by someone who meant it to outlast them. Don't starve it in a hurry, child. Left hungry, it will start drawing what it needs from whatever is nearest — the heat off your hearth first, then the sleep of whoever lives over it.

truth.speaker: Eloise
truth.text: There's no blight. Someone in that village struck a bargain with me — asked a favor, got exactly what they asked for. The price was always the second half of the deal, and they're pretending they forgot that part. The craft has been collecting on the debt ever since, out of their fields.

mediate_pitch.speaker: Eloise
mediate_pitch.text: Broker. That's a word for it. Go on, then, make your pitch. I'll hear it out. I've settled for less than I was owed before now.

options.text: Take a year of hearth-tending instead of whatever you were owed.

mediate_argue.speaker: Eloise
mediate_argue.text: A year, tending my hearth. Wood in winter, the kettle seen to the year round. It falls short of the debt I was owed. It might do.

mediated.speaker: Eloise
mediated.text: Fine. Tea first, and then it's settled. A year's honest work from a village that never meant to keep its favor. The woodpile is behind the house; tell them it starts there.

shop.speaker: Eloise
shop.text: Coin, then. Fine — not everyone wants to owe me something bigger. Take what you need and go.

options.text: The herb sachet, sewn shut. (6 gold)
That warded bead you're not selling. (16 gold)
The travel-stone under the cloth. It already knows the road to Invrisil. (18 gold)

effects.toast: The stone is warm and it keeps turning a little north in your hand. Ask the Door for Invrisil now and it will know what you mean.

options.text: That pinch of warding salt, for the threshold.
That dark red draught, for the road. (10 gold)

bought.speaker: Eloise
bought.text: Sold. Don't come back asking for a refund because it didn't work the way you hoped. And keep it out of the damp.

stone_sold.speaker: Eloise
stone_sold.text: That stone's walked the Invrisil road more times than I have. Keep it in a dry pocket, on the side you don't fall on. Don't lose it before you get there.

witch_ask._comment: #396: the ask STARTS the_makings, one-shot on its own counter. The bank is here and not on the hub row because that row's hide_when slot holds the drove_off_collectors exclusion, and a second key there would AND (dialogue.gd _meets), showing the offer to force-path players.
witch_ask.speaker: Eloise
witch_ask.text: Anyone can learn the shape of it. Hats. Herbs, mostly, if I'm honest. Words said over water come later. But the craft asks a question of you first, before any of that.

makings_brief.speaker: Eloise
makings_brief.text: Craft isn't told, child. It's done. Three things, then. Fill the pot by my door with what the hollow gives you. Tend something that can't thank you for it. Then come sit my kettle, and we'll see what you felt while you worked.

makings_chores.speaker: Eloise
makings_chores.text: Every witch you'll ever fear got that way doing chores with her whole heart in them. The chore is the least of it. What you carry while you do it is the craft.

makings_kettle.speaker: Eloise
makings_kettle.text: Pot filled. A lamb standing sound that wasn't. And you, back at my table with your hands smelling of both. Sit. The kettle's been waiting on you, not the water.

witch_lesson._comment: witch_lessons (FROZEN) stays the ONLY craft bank point, spent on its own hide_when. #396 adds both beat counters, so a legacy save holding it sees nothing new.
witch_lesson.speaker: Eloise
witch_lesson.text: Why did the debt get paid, child? Think past the how of it. Why. You sat at my table and went looking for the ending where nobody bled. That's the question, answered before I asked it. The craft grows from what a person already is. Mine roots in kindness.

options.text: Then teach me the first of it.
I need to think on that.

witch_taught.speaker: Eloise
witch_taught.text: Small things first. A remedy that means it — stir it thinking of the sick one, and never mind how the pot looks. My cauldron is yours when the fire's lit, and the inn's kettle will do in a pinch. Sleep on it, child. There's yarrow drying over the hearth; we'll start there.
